design_notes: Two axes (size x edit) yield 12 cells. Disk usage is a recorded metric, not a third axis: a disk tertile would triple the grid and leave most cells empty while four agents are still seeding.
Fitness is median wall time in milliseconds of the configured iteration loop (genome.loop: check, graph, or test) on that edit type. Lower is better. Spread is population stdev of the timed samples.

validate is not a gene. It is always cargo test with default LLVM rustc. A genome that fails the correctness gate (fast path and rustc must agree on broken edits; validate is the final signal) cannot occupy a cell.
Replace an elite only when the new median is at least fitness.min_gain_pct faster (default 3%) and correctness.ok is true. Seed an empty cell with the first passing evaluation.
Stop a cell after fitness.max_non_improving consecutive non-improving tries. Hill-climb restarts may re-seed a stopped cell with a new genome family.
Do not stack RUSTC_WRAPPER=nanocompile with sccache. Cranelift is a dev-backend gene only; rust-loop run strips it from validate.
Other agents write bench/archive/<sample>.json shards. Merge with `nanocompile map-elites merge` or `python3 tools/map_elites.py merge`.
